summary.headline: BCL Industries FY26 revenue INR2,913 crore, EBITDA INR251 crore (+18%), margin 8.6%; 150 KLPD Bathinda unit nearing commercial output.
summary.overview: BCL Industries reported FY26 total revenue of INR2,913 crore, with EBITDA up 18% YoY to INR251 crore and margin up 130 bps to 8.6%. Q4 PAT was INR126 crore, up 23% YoY at a 4.3% margin. Ethanol allocation from OMCs was lower than expected, so the company diverted output to ENA and SBF, which kept utilisation near full but pressured realisations. The packaged edible oil business was exited, while the refinery and trading businesses continued. The 150 KLPD Bathinda grain-based distillery is in testing, taking total installed capacity to 900 KLPD.

financial_highlights.change: FY26 revenue largely in line with FY25 despite packaged edible oil exit

financial_highlights.metric: Distillery EBITDA margin Q4 FY26 (as cited by analyst)

financial_highlights.value: about INR300-335 crore incl. fund-based and non-fund based
less than 7%; INR120 crore on interest subvention at about 4.25%

segments.name: Distillery (ENA, SBF, ethanol)
segments.commentary: Ethanol volume near 190,000 KL in FY26 with distillery EBITDA margin of 11.03%. ENA and SBF volumes rose about 74% to 53,000 KL as output was diverted from lower ethanol allocation. Management said about 50% of flexible capacity goes to ENA and SBF.

segments.name: Potable liquor (PML, Punjab Made Liquor)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 sales of almost 4.5 lakh cases, up 20% YoY. Punjab Special Whiskey relaunched in glass bottle and Punjab Raspberry added. Management cited 18-20% PML market growth.

segments.name: Refinery (edible oil and trading)
segments.commentary: Revenue under INR749 crore with EBITDA margin of 3.74% in FY26. Packaged edible oil exited; soft oil refinery continues, with bulk supply expected at INR700-800 crore per year.

segments.name: Biodiesel
segments.commentary: 75 KLPD capacity currently idle for biodiesel; plant run on vegetable oil refining instead. Company is enrolled as a biodiesel supplier with OMCs, awaiting a price revision.

guidance_outlook: 150 KLPD Bathinda unit: testing under way, rated capacity targeted by first week of July 2026; at least 75% utilisation expected from Q2 FY27.
Management expects FY27 revenue of about INR300 crore from the 150 KLPD unit at full utilisation.
Management expects EBITDA margins to be maintained at similar levels, with possible improvement from fixed overheads spread over higher capacity.
Svaksha Distillery 25% stake acquisition expected to complete by end June 2026, making it a wholly owned subsidiary.
Fatehabad 250 KLPD ethanol plant with 20 TPD CBG plant: approval steps expected to close in about a month; commissioning in about 2 years; CBG about 1 year after that.
Management aims to be a debt-free company within 5 years.
capex_capacity: Bathinda 150 KLPD grain-based distillery completed and in testing; total installed capacity to reach 900 KLPD.
Paddy straw boiler of 55 tonnes per hour added; company says it now meets 100% of steam and power needs.
Proposed Fatehabad 250 KLPD ethanol expansion, taking total capacity to about 1,150 KLPD; land and work started.
Biodiesel 75 KLPD capacity idle pending policy revision; no capex currently planned per management.
demand_pricing: Government evaluating E30 blending standards and E85/E100 flex fuel norms, which management says support medium to long-term OMC ethanol demand.
Lower-than-expected ethanol allocation forced diversion to ENA and SBF, where realisations were under pressure from competition.
Management says OMCs now find ethanol blending more profitable at higher crude prices, supporting additional demand.
ENA and SBF sold on cash-and-carry basis; OMC receivables cut to about 21 days.

qa_highlights.question: What are FY27 and FY28 revenue and EBITDA margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects about INR300 crore from the 150 KLPD unit at full utilisation and similar or slightly better EBITDA margins as overheads stay flat.

qa_highlights.question: Can the new 150 KLPD unit run at 100% in year one?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management expects at least 75% utilisation from Q2 FY27, with rated capacity by early July after a 15-day trial production.

qa_highlights.question: Can distillery EBITDA hold at 11.8% in Q4 given peers guide 12-15%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins should hold, citing the paddy straw boiler and consolidation of vegetable oil operations. Pure ethanol could reach 15% at full OMC allocation, but ENA/SBF are raw-material linked and not fixed-margin.

qa_highlights.question: What is the 3-5 year strategy and real estate exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: Real estate projects date from 2005-2010 and are winding down with no new projects. Focus is biofuel: Fatehabad ethanol, later CBG and sustainable aviation fuel, and a debt-free balance sheet within 5 years.

qa_highlights.question: What is net debt and cost of debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt about INR300-335 crore including fund and non-fund based; INR120 crore on interest subvention at about 4.25%; average cost below 7%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the OCF improvement sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said working capital release is not one-off: no capex currently, ENA/SBF cash-and-carry sales, OMC receivables cut to 21 days, and edible oil inventory liquidation adds to it.

qa_highlights.question: Why exit packaged edible oil and sell land?
qa_highlights.answer: City unit had to move due to red-category restrictions. Machines were shifted or sold, and about 18 acres of city land is being sold for about INR30 crore. Proceeds go to cash and expansion.

risks_watch: Ethanol allocation from OMCs remains below capacity; ENA/SBF pricing is competitive and raw-material linked.
Ramp-up of the 150 KLPD Bathinda unit to 75% by Q2 FY27 and rated capacity by early July 2026.
Timing of biodiesel price revision by OMCs; the 75 KLPD plant stays idle until then.
Grain (maize and rice) price pass-through is lagged in ENA/SBF; management says pass-through is not immediate.
Fatehabad 250 KLPD expansion and CBG timelines (about 2 years and 3 years) depend on policy and technology.
Recovery of residual edible oil inventory within 4-6 months and sale of 18-acre land parcel.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the capacity and policy outlook, but guarded on specifics: management declined to commit on biodiesel pricing and distillery margins, citing commodity risk and government timing.

We don't want to borrow money and launch this IMFL business Pan-India because that will be a very high cost for the company or maybe high risk for that.
And we ha ve positioned ourselves, within 5 years, we should be a total debt -free company, which we are focusing on.
